question: If 4 men or 6 boys can finish a piece of work in 20 days, then in how many days can 6 men and 11 boys finish the same work?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Efficiency Ratio: 4 Men = 6 Boys ⇒ 2 Men = 3 Boys.

Convert Men into Boys: 6 Men = (3 ÷ 2) × 6 = 9 Boys.

Total Group Requirement: 6 Men + 11 Boys = 9 Boys + 11 Boys = 20 Boys.

Using M₁D₁ = M₂D₂ ⇒ 6 Boys × 20 Days = 20 Boys × Days.

Required Days = 120 ÷ 20 = 6 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 6 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by 4 Men = 20 days ⇒ Time taken by 1 Man = 4 × 20 = 80 days.

Time taken by 6 Boys = 20 days ⇒ Time taken by 1 Boy = 6 × 20 = 120 days.

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = LCM of individual days; Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Days.

**Calculations:**

⇒ Efficiency of 6 Men = 6 × 3 = 18 units/day.

⇒ Efficiency of 11 Boys = 11 × 2 = 22 units/day.

⇒ Combined Efficiency (6 Men + 11 Boys) = 18 + 22 = 40 units/day.

⇒ Required Time = Total Work ÷ Combined Efficiency

⇒ Required Time = 240 ÷ 40 = 6 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 6 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Man-Days Formula

The relationship between men, days, and hours is given by (M₁ × D₁ × H₁) ÷ W₁ = (M₂ × D₂ × H₂) ÷ W₂.

Efficiency and Time Relationship

Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken to complete the work (Efficiency ∝ 1 ÷ Time).

Work and Wages

Wages are always distributed in the ratio of the work done by each person, which is the product of efficiency and time.</p
